media.rationale: ZBar, xxd, file and foremost are short task-driven identification/conversion/carving lookups. They support triage but do not each justify another long lesson; keep each existing reference and consult it when QR, hex, unknown-format or carving evidence appears.

Image channels and integrity remain an important reference family. zsteg does not replace visual bit-plane inspection or PNG/JPEG validation. Keep ImageMagick/G’MIC channel manipulation, StegSolve bit planes and pngcheck/jpeginfo integrity references; prioritise these on a challenge with damaged headers, CRC errors or visible channel clues. Installed fork/version remains relevant.

MediaInfo and SoX_ng overlap common inspection covered by FFmpeg/Audacity; keep reference-only to avoid repeat lessons. SSTV is a distinct narrow encoding and must remain discoverable, but the decoder-versus-PySSTV package mismatch prevents treating execution as a dependable flight prerequisite.

OpenStego-specific and SNOW whitespace extraction are recognisable narrow branches. Retain existing direct references and lookup triggers; generic PNG LSB or audio study does not imply mastery of these formats.
AperiSolve is reference-only because local deployment preparation is substantial and its analyzer set overlaps individually taught tools; public upload is forbidden for event artifacts.
Sonic Visualiser is covered by the free reading alternative and optional audio investigation, rather than a duplicate full audio-editor lesson. Its v5.2.1 reference matches the workbook version.

web-network: Burp/curl/ffuf form one inspect-replay-enumerate workflow; Feroxbuster/Gobuster/Katana stay reference-only to avoid repeating discovery introductions.
SQLmap and jwt_tool are vulnerability-specific lookups after identifying relevant SQL/JWT evidence; PayloadsAllTheThings remains indexed reference, not cover-to-cover reading.
Nmap gets a short state/service refresher; RustScan/Legion repeat reconnaissance setup, and Impacket/Metasploit/Hydra require a specific service/target, so retain their exact approved references.

CAN utilities/cannelloni and RTP tools need matching bus/media artifacts; wireless Aircrack/hcxtools need captures and protocol prerequisites. Keep references rather than requiring hardware/live work on a plane.
Subfinder is the sole OSINT entry in this lane and needs network-backed passive sources; explicitly reference-only.
tcpdump and Zui overlap the selected packet workflow; retain their tool-specific references. OpenVPN setup and Chrome DevTools remain utility lookups.

Community manual tools are usable; Professional scanner, Collaborator, full Intruder and saved project files must not be implied by the training plan. Supplemental ffufme/Docker home practice does not expand event approval.

forensics.rationale: Keep ALEAPP/iLEAPP/mac_apt reference-only: input acquisition formats and OS versions determine useful parsers, and no corresponding evidence set is assumed. Trigger: a supplied Android/iOS/macOS extraction. First consult the row repository for accepted input layout and output reports; generic disk lessons do not teach these tools.

forensics.family: Browser, SQLite recovery and encrypted databases
forensics.rationale: SQLite schema/query training is transferable but not a substitute for Hindsight browser artifacts, FQLite deleted-record recovery or SQLCipher keys/settings. Keep these interfaces reference-only; use the input-specific parser when ordinary SQLite inspection cannot answer the question. Preserve supplied database companions; no guarantee deleted records survive.

Autopsy and the MFTECmd/Chainsaw lessons cover artifact selection and output reasoning, not standalone RegRipper, Plaso or Hayabusa operation. Keep row docs: choose RegRipper for a specific hive, Plaso for cross-artifact timelines, Hayabusa as the alternate EVTX workflow rather than learning two event hunters during the first pass.

Volatility 2, its profiles/plugins and Volatility 3 symbols/plugins are separate compatibility paths. The core teaches only approved windows-31 Volatility 3. Linux symbol generation, SSH-session recovery and credential artifacts stay reference-only until the evidence requires them; no promise that installed plugins support a particular image.

forensics.family: Containers, mailbox and alternative recovery utilities
forensics.rationale: Keep EWF/qemu-img/ESE/PFF and bulk/carving/FAT-check docs as format-triggered references. They solve different obstacles, not mandatory extra stages for every challenge. Filesystem-aware TSK triage comes first; carving may lose names/paths and cannot guarantee recovery.

forensics.family: Lightweight viewers, text extraction and repository evidence
forensics.rationale: Preserve each row reference without a separate course. qpdf covers structural PDF inspection; it does not teach every viewer or mutool. strings retains its GNU documentation after the old TSK lesson is replaced. Git/Gitleaks are evidence-specific history/search workflows, not part of the disk-memory sequence.

reverse.rationale: dnSpyEx is the sole selected managed-code routing reference. Native Ghidra/GDB proficiency does not establish .NET expertise; keep a short reference until a real managed assembly warrants a separate lab.

JADX orientation covers APK/DEX and manifest/resource navigation. Apktool, dex2jar, Android Studio, Bytecode Viewer and Fernflower retain exact approved-row references; separate overlapping introductions would crowd out practice. APK modification/emulation and native JNI need a separate prepared lab.

pyinstxtractor-ng is a short extraction reference; pycdc/uncompyle6/unpyc3 remain bytecode-version-specific references, not interchangeable guarantees. Read supported input versions rather than inferring support from the host Python runtime.
Ghidra and stock GDB provide the core workflow. x64dbg/OllyDbg/Cutter/radare2 and GEF/peda/pwndbg remain approved reference choices; no need to relearn the same branch task in every interface.

capa/FLOSS/YARA establish static triage roles. Existing approved references for Didier tools, oletools, FakeNet-NG, AutoIt and format-specific unpackers remain available; no live-malware plane lab is required or proposed.

angr/ROPgadget remain references for a challenge that actually needs path constraints or gadgets. General native input-check recovery is a prerequisite; adding advanced courses without a diagnostic gap would dilute this refresher.

crypto-foundations.rationale: crypto-attacks remains a searchable implementation/test-vector library. Specialized lattice tuning is outside the scheduled refresher; removal from study does not remove approval or its inventory reference.
factordb-python is network-dependent and unnecessary for the tiny local RSA fixture. Keep reference only; approval is not authorization to transmit event challenge material.

hlextend and padding-oracle-attacker are pattern-specific helpers needing a vulnerable construction/oracle. General RSA/hash exercises do not cover them; retain exact upstream references and state this gap instead of claiming broad cryptographic mastery.
PARI/GP is an alternative number-theory runtime; Sage/Python cover this block’s arithmetic. Use the existing reference if a supplied solver specifically needs GP.
hashid is triage, not proof of algorithm identity; check context and known format examples before selecting a cracking mode.
rockyou is a wordlist, not a separate tool course. The three-word fixture teaches candidate handling without downloading a large corpus.
OpenSSL remains reference-only for explicit cipher, key, IV and salt parameters; the curated block does not claim AES/OpenSSL coverage.
multimon-ng signal decoding needs an appropriate recorded signal and modulation knowledge; reference-only pending a matching challenge, not covered by the crypto refresh.
GTFOBins and HackTricks offline copies are broad lookups, not sequential course material. Preserve references and use matching sections when a concrete binary or technique appears.

Runtimes, editors, archive utilities and environment/data helpers are supporting tools. Preserve every existing row-specific reference; use the participant’s familiar editor/runtime and a small archive exercise rather than parallel language or editor courses. Python 2 differs from the Python 3.8+ inverse example.

schedule.title: Identify and decode files
schedule.outcome: Choose a first inspection operation and validate decoded output.
schedule.selection: Read CyberChef recipe order, three ExifTool reading examples, Binwalk scan/extract and zsteg channel-selection examples. The CyberChef video is an alternative, not extra work.
schedule.diagnostic: Explain encoding versus encryption and why a signature is only a lead.
schedule.preparation: Local CyberChef and HxD/xxd only for execution; all paper inputs and the tiny PCAP are bundled.
schedule.assessment: Round-trip Base64, identify the capture header, and state an independent validation check.

schedule.title: Reconstruct network evidence
schedule.prerequisites: Block 1; basic IP/port and request/response concepts.
schedule.outcome: Follow a complete conversation and reproduce selected fields.
schedule.selection: Read official display filters/Follow Stream and TShark -r/-Y/-T fields. Use the same tiny capture for GUI/CLI; Zeek quickstart is optional depth within the block.
schedule.diagnostic: Explain display versus capture filters and stream reassembly.
schedule.preparation: Bundled http-demo.pcap; Wireshark/TShark for execution. Zeek needs a separately working install.
schedule.assessment: Match the supplied endpoint/URI/body answer key; explain client versus server direction.

schedule.title: Interpret filesystem and Windows artifacts
schedule.prerequisites: Blocks 1–2; sectors/bytes and file metadata are distinct concepts.
schedule.outcome: Keep recovery coordinates straight and avoid unsupported attribution.
schedule.selection: Read TSK fls/mmls/icat arguments, Autopsy case→source→ingest→export, and MFTECmd author documentation or selected video chapters. Use SQLite schema sections if time remains.
schedule.diagnostic: Distinguish sector offset, block index and metadata address.
schedule.preparation: Both paper cases are bundled: coordinates, file listing and normalized journal rows. Optional Autopsy execution needs a prepared benign image or logical-file folder.
schedule.assessment: Compute both offsets; write the recovery commands; group journal rows by full identity and explain rename/deletion and attribution limits.

schedule.title: Reason from memory artifacts
schedule.prerequisites: Block 3; process IDs and parent relationships.
schedule.outcome: Read pslist/pstree and distinguish missing prerequisites from negative findings.
schedule.selection: Read official process tutorial; video is optional instead of repeated introduction. Compare plugin output structure with the supplied process table.
schedule.diagnostic: Explain Volatility 2 profiles versus Volatility 3 symbols.
schedule.preparation: Both synthetic process cases are bundled. Tool execution separately requires an image, working Volatility and pre-cached matching symbols.
schedule.assessment: Reconstruct both process cases, identify missing parents, distinguish same-named processes, pair hypotheses with evidence and write the tutorial command sequence.

schedule.title: Recover a native input check
schedule.prerequisites: Basic C branches, arguments and strings; skim source syntax first if rusty.
schedule.outcome: Relate source, disassembly and decompiler output, then verify a hypothesis.
schedule.selection: Use Ghidra import/decompiler/references/function graph and the benign companion. Choose at most one video for orientation; spend the rest on the included C program.
schedule.diagnostic: Explain strcmp returning zero and how a branch uses the result.
schedule.preparation: Bundled C source; GCC/GDB for executed route, Ghidra optional. Save the published companion source/disassembly for the paper transfer exercise.
schedule.assessment: Predict all three output/status cases; compare your recovered condition with source.

schedule.title: Test static-analysis claims
schedule.prerequisites: Block 5; strings, conditions and basic file formats.
schedule.outcome: Write a specific rule and treat extraction/capability labels as evidence leads.
schedule.selection: Read capa default/verbose output, FLOSS string types and YARA strings/conditions/fullword. Format-routing references are short optional lookups.
schedule.diagnostic: Distinguish decoded strings from executed behavior.
schedule.preparation: Bundled harmless text files and rule; YARA only for execution. No malware samples needed.
schedule.assessment: Distinguish full-word and substring matches, check the missing-marker case, and name a justified next check for a capa/FLOSS finding.

schedule.title: Replay controlled HTTP changes
schedule.outcome: Change one request field, compare responses and avoid false discovery conclusions.
schedule.selection: Read Repeater steps, curl headers/cookies/POST and ffuf FUZZ/filter examples. Video substitutes for the first orientation; no hosted lab required.
schedule.diagnostic: Write a GET and explain path versus header changes.
schedule.preparation: Bundled static target served by Python on loopback; curl/Burp Community for execution. Paper requests need no server or account.
schedule.assessment: Show 200 versus 404 after one path change; explain wildcard-response filtering.

schedule.title: Check crypto and password assumptions
schedule.outcome: Derive a toy RSA result and map candidate testing to the right tool.
schedule.selection: Read RSA prerequisites and initial Sage arithmetic; do hashcat dictionary OR John wordlist introduction. Use bkcrack metadata/conditions as a separate optional branch.
schedule.diagnostic: Explain n/e/d, hash candidates and ZipCrypto versus AES.
schedule.preparation: Included Python 3 toy inputs need no Sage or network. Optional bkcrack execution needs its exact public archive and installed binary.
schedule.assessment: Recover 42, identify cat, and state when RSA/ZIP attacks do not apply.

schedule.title: Close one specialist gap
schedule.prerequisites: Choose based on a failed diagnostic, not novelty.
schedule.outcome: Apply one narrowly scoped unfamiliar workflow.
schedule.selection: Choose exactly one worksheet branch: audio-window tradeoff, managed-format routing, or SQLite schema/query. Other niche families remain indexed references.
schedule.diagnostic: Explain the chosen task in two sentences before reading.
schedule.preparation: All three paper branches have inputs and answers; actual audio/decompiler use requires a separately prepared file/tool.
schedule.assessment: Check the specified tradeoff, format routing, or query order; record one failure mode.

schedule.title: Transfer without instructions
schedule.outcome: Repeat two workflows independently and record remaining gaps.
schedule.selection: No new resource; close the notes and repeat one interpretation task and one executable task.
schedule.diagnostic: Name three inputs, approved tools and first non-destructive actions.
schedule.preparation: Use included exercises; mark paper-only attempts honestly.
schedule.assessment: Assess tool choice, input preservation, correct operation and justified interpretation; record corrections.
